records.name: Teardrops Liquid Language of the Heart
records.summary: A faith-based coaching group that teaches people to treat tears as a signal for change. It offers a short teaching each Tuesday morning and a monthly live women's gathering on Facebook and YouTube.
records.what_you_do: Watch or join the live Tuesday teaching or the monthly women's table online, and reach out through the site's contact form to share what is on your heart.

schedule.text: A teaching every Tuesday at 6:00 AM, and a women's table on the third Thursday of each month at 7:00 PM, live on Facebook and YouTube

cost.text: No fee listed on the page

first_step.how: Tune in to the next Tuesday morning teaching or the third Thursday women's table, live on Facebook or YouTube
first_step.basis: The sessions are public and live online, and the page does not mention signing up.

records.notes: Site has no dated items. The only year is a 2026 copyright footer, which is not evidence, so probably_active rests on a working site with no dates. The site never names Philadelphia. The only Philadelphia link is the IRS filing address, which looks like a residence apartment and was not published. Reviewer should confirm it serves Philadelphia before it goes live. 'When Tears Speak' is marked coming soon, so it is not listed.

records.name: Unity Recovery
records.summary: A peer-run recovery organization with a Philadelphia presence. It offers free one-on-one peer support, recovery meetings held online, life skills workshops, and volunteer roles for people in recovery.
records.what_you_do: Request one-on-one peer support, join the digital recovery meetings, take a life skills workshop, or sign up to volunteer.

schedule.text: Digital recovery meetings run on a weekly schedule the site posts. The page does not list meeting days or times.

locations.label: Community centers in Philadelphia, plus telephone and video support

cost.text: Free. The group says it never charges a fee.

first_step.how: Use the Request Support page on the website, or call 267.748.2454, or email contact@unityrecovery.org
first_step.basis: Services are free and open to the public, with a request form and a phone line on the site.

records.notes: Newest dated item on the site is a November 25, 2025 article. The upcoming events list was empty. Footer reads Copyright 2022, which is not used as evidence. Meeting times are not on the page, so ask through the request page. The group also runs sites in Pittsburgh and Texas, which this record does not cover. Discord invite recorded as a social link.

records.name: Unorthodox Therapy
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that offers women affordable, non-clinical support through monthly peer groups for mothers, married women, singles, single mothers, and parents of autistic children. Some groups meet online and some in person.
records.what_you_do: Pick the monthly group that fits your life stage, such as motherhood or singles, and sign up through its register link to talk with other women in a supportive circle.

schedule.text: Monthly groups on set days: Motherhood on the first Monday, Marriage on the second Tuesday, Singles on the third Wednesday, Single Mama on the fourth Thursday, and ASD Parenting on the fifth Friday. The dates on the site are listed inconsistently.

cost.text: Most events are $25 or less. Some free healing sessions are offered, capped at 10 people.

first_step.how: Pick a group on the community page and use its Register link, which goes to the scheduling page
first_step.basis: Each group has a published sign up page and the groups are open to women and parents.

records.notes: Dates on the groups page conflict with each other. Motherhood is shown as August 2026 and as fall 2026, Marriage as September 2026 and winter 2025, and SALT is marked season ended April 2025 with next season 2027. Status and last sign of life use the newest 2026 date shown. Unbecoming six-week series dates are unclear (2026 and 2027 both appear), so it is left out of the schedule. Legal name Unorthodox Therapy Inc. Homepage describes the group as a Philadelphia based 501(c)(3).

records.name: Village on the Ridge
records.notes: The website typed on the IRS filing (www.villageontheridge.org) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to the fetch tool. The page could not be read. It was not retried or worked around. No summary, categories or interests were written, so this record is held back. The IRS filing gives a Philadelphia zip (19128). Needs a manual check from a browser or a search by name.

records.name: W.B. Saul Home and School Association
records.summary: The parent group for W.B. Saul High School. Parents, guardians and students plan school volunteer work, run fundraisers, and speak up for the school at meetings held in person and on Zoom.
records.what_you_do: Come to a general meeting, join a committee, or share a talent with the group. Volunteers must complete school district clearance first.

schedule.text: General meetings on Thursdays from 6 to 7 pm, in person and on Zoom, about once a month during the school year. A monthly Zoom Q and A with school leadership runs on Fridays at 2 pm.

locations.label: W.B. Saul High School (in person meetings)

cost.text: Membership form is free. The group suggests a donation of $5 to $30 per family, and any amount is accepted.

first_step.how: Come to the next general body meeting on Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 6 pm, in person or on Zoom, or fill out the membership form on the website
first_step.basis: Parents, guardians and students are welcome at meetings, and the site has a membership form.

records.notes: Judgment call for review: the brief lists booster clubs for one school as hide (private). Published because this is a school parent association whose meetings are open to parents, guardians and students, and it has a public membership form. Reviewer may flip to hide if the owner treats school parent groups as private. The site calls the October 15, 2026 meeting the last meeting of the academic year, but its schedule lists June 11, 2026 as the final meeting. The street address is from the IRS filing, not the group's site. The Zoom meeting IDs on the site were deliberately not recorded. Legal name W B Saul Home & School Association.

records.name: Building Brighter Futures
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports children and young people up to age 21 who are in or entering foster care in Philadelphia. It collects Care Kits of hygiene supplies and runs holiday events and family sponsorships.
records.what_you_do: Donate money or hygiene supplies for Care Kits, sponsor a family or child for a holiday, or contact the office to ask how to help at events.

locations.label: Philadelphia, PA (no street address on the site)

cost.text: No event cost listed. Donations and sponsorships are welcome.

first_step.how: Donate through the Givebutter link on the website, or call or email the office to ask how to help with Care Kits or events
first_step.basis: The site lists donations and contact options, but does not say how to volunteer or sign up for events.

records.notes: Newest dated item is the December 14, 2024 Christmas event. The footer reads Copyright 2025, which is not evidence. Office hours on the site are Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm. The email domain on the site (BuildingBrighterFuture.org) differs from the website domain (buildingbrighterfutures.net). Both are recorded as published.

records.name: Giving Hope Foundation International
records.notes: No usable website. The IRS filing's website field reads as a service description ('Service provider of behavioral and home care services'), which is not a web address. The one search for this name found no page for a Philadelphia group with this name. The closest matches were other Giving Hope and Hope groups in Maryland, York and Philadelphia, none confirmed as this one. The filing's wording suggests a home care business rather than a community group, so the reviewer may move it to not_a_group. No summary, categories or interests written, so this record is held back. IRS address is on South 63rd Street, zip 19142.

records.name: God's Army International Prayer Ministries
records.summary: A faith ministry that has served dinner and toiletries to men at a Philadelphia shelter. It also runs meal programs for children and older people in Liberia.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for updates on the website, or send a question through the Contact Us page to ask how to help with the shelter meals.

cost.text: No program fee listed. The site has a donation option.

first_step.how: Sign up for updates through the website's sign up form, or send a question through the Contact Us page
first_step.basis: The site has sign up and contact options but does not describe volunteering, meetings or how to attend.

records.notes: The only dated item on the site is a photo caption for a donation received on May 13, 2020, so status is dormant. The copyright 2020 footer is not counted. The Liberia programs are outside Philadelphia; the Philadelphia link is the shelter program and the IRS filing address. The site uses several name variants. No phone or email found. Dormant is a status, not a hide reason, so the record is published for the reviewer to decide.

records.name: Heavenly Made Blessings
records.summary: A Philadelphia charity that supports families, children and childcare providers through mentoring, coaching, training workshops and scholarships for childcare tuition. It also holds community drives and fundraisers.
records.what_you_do: Ask about a mentoring or coaching spot, a training workshop, a childcare scholarship, or a volunteer shift, or give a donation.

cost.text: Program costs are not listed. Scholarships and donations are offered.

first_step.how: Call 267-237-0706 or email heavenlymadeblessings@gmail.com to ask which mentoring, workshop or volunteer spots are open
first_step.basis: Anyone can reach the group by phone or email, and the site lists mentoring, workshop and volunteer pages.

records.notes: The site has no dated events or news. The only year is a footer reading 2022 to 2026, which is not evidence. Status is probably_active because the site is working. The volunteer and scholarship pages are linked but were not read. Legal name Heavenly Made Blessings. The address is a P.O. Box from the site, not a meeting place.

records.name: Industrial University of Africa
records.notes: Sells paid distance courses, for example $15 to $45 per course and $15 per credit hour for an MBA. The site is c/o MI&I Partners in Washington, DC. No Philadelphia program or community program is listed. The IRS filing lists a Philadelphia P.O. box. This is a business, so not_a_group. It could also be out_of_area. Not published.

records.name: International Helping Hands Ministries
records.notes: The site shows only the words 'This site is under development.' It has no programs, dates, contact details or way to join. Hidden as private because there is no public way in. Re-check later. If the group launches public programs, run tier 1 again.

records.name: Millsburg Liberia Development Project
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives computers to children from low-income families so they can do schoolwork and learn about technology. It also promotes education and training in struggling communities.
records.what_you_do: Ask about receiving or donating a computer, donate through the website, or subscribe to the newsletter.

cost.text: No cost listed for joining, donating or receiving a computer

first_step.how: Call 267-888-0230 to ask about receiving or donating a computer, or use the subscribe form on the website
first_step.basis: The site has a subscribe form and a phone number, but does not explain how families are chosen or how to donate.

records.notes: No dated events or news on the page. The only year is a 2010 copyright line, which is not evidence. probably_active comes from the rule for working sites with no dates, but the 2010 copyright suggests the site may be stale. Reviewer may prefer unknown or dormant. The Get Involved, Donate and Newsletter pages were linked but not read. The Facebook page is linked but not read. The Philadelphia address is the site's own address.

records.name: Minority Center for Participation and Empowerment
records.summary: A community organization that works to reduce violence and poverty and to improve living conditions for underserved communities. Its listed programs include literacy, after school, mentorship, vocational training and youth services.
records.what_you_do: Ask for services through the intake form on the website, or contact the group to ask about its after school and mentoring programs.

cost.text: No program cost listed. The site has a donate button.

first_step.how: Fill out the intake form on the website, or use the Contact page to ask about the after school or mentoring program
first_step.basis: The site lists an intake form and a contact page, but the programs are not described and the pages read do not explain how to join.

records.notes: Programs are listed by menu label only, for example 'female emp', 'SummerC' and 'elderly', with no descriptions. No dates with a year and no address or phone were found on the pages read. Several page addresses start with copy-of, which suggests a draft site. probably_active comes from the rule for a working site with no dates. The Contact page, intake form and afterschool page were not read. Board names were not recorded. The summary leans on menu labels, so the reviewer should verify the programs before this goes live. The IRS filing lists a Philadelphia address.
